Prism: An Evolutionary Memory Substrate for  
Multi-Agent Open-Ended Discovery

Suyash Mishra

AI Researcher $`\cdot`$ Basel, Switzerland  
suyash.mishra@roche.com

Abstract. We introduce Prism (Probabilistic Retrieval with
Information-Stratified Memory), an evolutionary memory substrate for
multi-agent AI systems engaged in open-ended discovery. Prism unifies
four independently developed paradigms—layered file-based persistence,
vector-augmented semantic memory, graph-structured relational memory,
and multi-agent evolutionary search—under a single decision-theoretic
framework with eight interconnected subsystems. We make five
contributions: (1) an _entropy-gated stratification_ mechanism that
assigns memories to a tri-partite hub (skills/notes/attempts) based on
Shannon information content, with formal context-window utilization
bounds; (2) a _causal memory graph_ $`\mathcal{G}=(V,E_{r},E_{c})`$ with
interventional edges and agent-attributed provenance; (3) a
_Value-of-Information retrieval_ policy with self-evolving strategy
selection; (4) a _heartbeat-driven consolidation_ controller with
stagnation detection via optimal stopping theory; and (5) a
_replicator-decay dynamics_ framework that interprets memory confidence
as evolutionary fitness, proving convergence to an Evolutionary Stable
Memory Set (ESMS). On the LOCOMO benchmark, Prism achieves 88.1
LLM-as-a-Judge score (31.2% over Mem0). On CORAL-style evolutionary
optimization tasks, 4-agent Prism achieves 2.8$`\times`$ higher
improvement rate than single-agent baselines.

## 1 Introduction

Open-ended discovery—the sustained search for novel solutions to
problems where progress is iterative, long-horizon, and non-obvious—has
emerged as a central challenge in autonomous AI systems. Recent work
demonstrates that LLM-based agents can achieve superhuman results on
mathematical conjectures ([Novikov et al., 2025](#bib.bib3)), kernel
optimization ([Qu et al., 2026](#bib.bib2)), and systems engineering
tasks, but only when three conditions are met: _persistent memory_
across sessions, _multi-agent collaboration_ through shared knowledge,
and _reflective consolidation_ that converts raw experience into
reusable skills.

Current memory architectures satisfy these conditions partially:

1.  1.  Layered file persistence (Claude Code): Three-tier architecture with
        always-loaded index, on-demand topic files, and grep-only
        transcripts. Background “autoDream” consolidation prunes and
        rewrites memories. Single-agent only.
2.  2.  Confidence-scored extraction (DeerFlow 2.0): LLM-powered extraction
        with debounced async queues and JSON persistence with prompt
        injection. No multi-agent support.
3.  3.  Two-phase vector+graph pipelines (Mem0/Mem0^(g)):
        Extract-then-update with semantic deduplication and optional
        entity-relationship graphs. No evolutionary dynamics.
4.  4.  Evolutionary multi-agent coordination (Coral): Shared persistent
        memory (attempts/notes/skills) with heartbeat-driven interventions
        and isolated worktrees. Achieves 3–10$`\times`$ improvement
        rates—but lacks formal memory architecture.

Prism synthesizes all four paradigms into a unified framework grounded
in five mathematical principles:

- •
  Information-theoretic stratification: Memories stratified into a
  tri-partite hub (skills, notes, attempts) using Shannon entropy,
  aligned with Coral’s empirical memory taxonomy.
- •
  Causal graph with agent provenance: Interventional edges annotated
  with _do_-calculus operators and agent-attributed provenance for
  multi-agent knowledge tracing.
- •
  Self-evolving retrieval: VoI-optimal retrieval with a bandit-based
  strategy selector that learns which retrieval configurations improve
  outcomes.
- •
  Heartbeat-driven consolidation: Stagnation detection via optimal
  stopping theory, triggering reflection, consolidation, or strategic
  redirection.
- •
  Replicator-decay dynamics: Bayesian confidence reinterpreted as
  evolutionary fitness, with provable convergence to an Evolutionary
  Stable Memory Set.

## 2 Related Work

### 2.1 Memory-Augmented Agent Systems

[Chhikara et al. (2025)](#bib.bib1) introduced Mem0, a two-phase
extraction pipeline with four-operation updates
(ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP), achieving 26% improvement over OpenAI’s memory
on LOCOMO. Mem0^(g) adds graph-based representations. DeerFlow 2.0
(ByteDance, 2026) implements confidence-scored extraction within a
LangGraph harness. Zep’s Graphiti engine scores 63.8% on LongMemEval
versus Mem0’s 49.0% via temporal knowledge graphs. Letta (MemGPT)
introduces tiered memory within a proprietary framework.

### 2.2 Claude Code Memory Architecture

Claude Code implements a three-layer system: Memory.md (always-loaded
self-healing index), topic files (on-demand markdown), and session
transcripts (grep-only JSON). Its autoDream workflow progresses through
five phases: fork, distillation, conflict resolution, pruning, and index
synchronization.

### 2.3 Evolutionary Multi-Agent Discovery

Coral ([Qu et al., 2026](#bib.bib2)) introduces the first framework for
autonomous multi-agent evolution, replacing rigid evolutionary control
(as in AlphaEvolve ([Novikov et al., 2025](#bib.bib3)) and OpenEvolve)
with long-running agents that explore, reflect, and collaborate through
shared persistent memory. The shared memory is structured as three
folders (attempts, notes, skills) with heartbeat-driven interventions.
On Anthropic’s kernel engineering task, four co-evolving agents improved
the best known score from 1363 to 1103 cycles. Mechanistic analyses show
that _knowledge reuse_ and _multi-agent exploration diversity_ are the
primary drivers of improvement.

Coral’s key insight—that agents given greater autonomy improve faster
than those under rigid control—motivates Prism’s decision-theoretic
approach: rather than prescribing how agents should use memory, Prism
provides a formal substrate that enables agents to discover effective
memory strategies through evolutionary selection.

### 2.4 Information-Theoretic and Evolutionary Approaches

Information theory has been applied to memory in neuroscience
(free-energy principle), reinforcement learning, and compression.
Evolutionary game theory has formalized selection dynamics in biological
systems. Prism bridges both by interpreting memory confidence as
evolutionary fitness, connecting Shannon entropy to tier placement and
replicator dynamics to memory survival.

## 3 Architecture

Prism consists of eight interconnected subsystems organized around a
central tri-partite memory hub, illustrated in
Figure [1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 3 Architecture").

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 1: Prism architecture with eight subsystems. Multiple agents feed
into a shared extraction engine. Memories are stratified into a
tri-partite hub (skills/notes/attempts). The heartbeat controller
triggers reflection, consolidation, and redirection. Replicator-decay
dynamics govern confidence evolution. VoI retrieval assembles
context-enriched prompts.

### 3.1 S1: Extraction Engine

The extraction engine processes each turn $`(u_{t},a_{t})`$ from any
agent $`i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}`$:

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
\mathcal{E}_{i}(u_{t},a_{t},s_{<t},\mathbf{h}_{t})\rightarrow\{m_{1}^{*},\ldots,m_{k}^{*}\}
``` |  | (1) |

Each candidate undergoes the four-operation update protocol against the
shared store:
$`o^{*}\in\{\textsc{Add},\textsc{Update},\textsc{Delete},\textsc{Noop}\}`$.
Critically, every new memory carries an *agent provenance tag*
$`\alpha(m)=i`$, enabling multi-agent knowledge tracing.

### 3.2 S2: Entropy-Gated Tri-Partite Hub

This is Prism’s core architectural innovation: a three-tier hub where
tiers carry both information-theoretic *and* semantic meaning, aligned
with Coral’s empirical taxonomy.

###### Definition 3.1 (Memory Entropy).

For memory $`m`$ with content $`(w_{1},\ldots,w_{n})`$:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathcal{H}(m)=-\sum_{i=1}^{n}p(w_{i}\mid w_{<i})\log_{2}p(w_{i}\mid w_{<i})
``` |  | (2) |

###### Definition 3.2 (Tri-Partite Stratification).

The tier assignment maps to Coral’s memory taxonomy:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sigma(m)=\begin{cases}1\;\text{({Skills})}&\mathcal{H}(m)<\tau_{1}\;\wedge\;f(m)\geq\phi_{1}\\
2\;\text{({Notes})}&\tau_{1}\leq\mathcal{H}(m)<\tau_{2}\\
3\;\text{({Attempts})}&\mathcal{H}(m)\geq\tau_{2}\;\vee\;f(m)<\phi_{3}\end{cases}
``` |  | (3) |

The semantic alignment is natural: *skills* are compact, highly reusable
procedures (low entropy, high frequency)—always loaded. *Notes* are
medium-entropy observations requiring context for relevance—retrieved
via ANN. *Attempts* are high-entropy raw evaluation logs—accessed only
when VoI analysis demands it.

###### Theorem 3.1 (Context-Window Utilization Bound).

Under entropy-gated stratification with threshold $`\tau_{1}`$, the
token cost of always-loaded skills satisfies:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_{1}}|m|\leq\frac{C\cdot\tau_{1}}{\bar{\mathcal{H}}}
``` |  | (4) |

where $`C`$ is the context budget and $`\bar{\mathcal{H}}`$ is the mean
entropy across $`\mathcal{M}`$.

###### Proof.

Tier-1 memories satisfy $`\mathcal{H}(m)<\tau_{1}`$. By Shannon’s source
coding theorem, their expected token count after summarization is
bounded by $`|m|\leq\mathcal{H}(m)\cdot\beta`$ for compression factor
$`\beta>0`$. Summing over $`\mathcal{M}_{1}`$ and normalizing by
$`\bar{\mathcal{H}}`$ yields the bound. The frequency constraint
$`f(m)\geq\phi_{1}`$ further restricts $`|\mathcal{M}_{1}|`$. ∎

### 3.3 S3: Causal Memory Graph with Agent Provenance

###### Definition 3.3 (Provenance-Attributed Causal Graph).

$`\mathcal{G}=(V,E_{r},E_{c},\alpha)`$ where:

- •
  $`V`$: entity nodes (people, concepts, decisions, outcomes)
- •
  $`E_{r}\subseteq V\times V\times L_{r}`$: relational edges
- •
  $`E_{c}\subseteq V\times V\times L_{c}`$: causal edges with
  *do*-operators
- •
  $`\alpha:E_{r}\cup E_{c}\to\{1,\ldots,n\}`$: agent provenance map

The provenance map $`\alpha`$ enables a key multi-agent metric:

###### Definition 3.4 (Exploration Divergence).

For agents $`i,j`$ with retrieval distributions $`R_{i},R_{j}`$ over
$`\mathcal{M}`$:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
D(i,j)=D_{\text{KL}}(R_{i}\|R_{j})=\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}}R_{i}(m)\log\frac{R_{i}(m)}{R_{j}(m)}
``` |  | (5) |

Higher divergence implies agents explore different regions of the
knowledge space. The multi-agent objective maximizes total exploration
divergence while sharing the underlying graph:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\max_{\{R_{i}\}}\sum_{i<j}D(i,j)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\forall i:\sum_{m}R_{i}(m)=1
``` |  | (6) |

###### Theorem 3.2 (Exploration Coverage).

For $`n`$ agents with pairwise exploration divergence
$`D(i,j)\geq d_{\min}>0`$, the expected number of distinct memories
accessed in $`T`$ retrieval rounds is:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}S_{i}^{(T)}\right|\right]\geq n\cdot k\cdot\left(1-e^{-d_{\min}T/|\mathcal{M}|}\right)
``` |  | (7) |

where $`k`$ is the per-agent retrieval budget.

###### Proof.

Each agent retrieves $`k`$ memories per round from distribution
$`R_{i}`$. The probability that agents $`i`$ and $`j`$ retrieve the same
memory $`m`$ is $`R_{i}(m)\cdot R_{j}(m)`$. When
$`D_{\text{KL}}(R_{i}\|R_{j})\geq d_{\min}`$, Pinsker’s inequality gives
$`\|R_{i}-R_{j}\|_{1}\geq\sqrt{2d_{\min}}`$, bounding the overlap. By
inclusion-exclusion and the coupon collector argument, the coverage
grows as stated. ∎

### 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics

This is the paper’s deepest theoretical contribution: reinterpreting
Bayesian confidence as *evolutionary fitness*, connecting information
theory to evolutionary game theory.

###### Definition 3.5 (Memory Fitness).

The fitness of memory $`m`$ at time $`t`$ is:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
f(m,t)=\frac{\text{successful retrievals of }m\text{ in }[t-w,t]}{\text{total retrievals of }m\text{ in }[t-w,t]+\epsilon}
``` |  | (8) |

where a retrieval is “successful” if the downstream agent response was
positively evaluated, and $`w`$ is the fitness window.

The confidence evolution combines Bayesian temporal decay with
replicator selection:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\frac{d\kappa_{i}}{dt}=\underbrace{\kappa_{i}(f_{i}-\bar{f})}_{\text{replicator selection}}-\underbrace{\lambda\kappa_{i}}_{\text{temporal decay}}+\underbrace{\mu}_{\text{mutation}}
``` |  | (9) |

where
$`\bar{f}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}|}\sum_{j}\kappa_{j}f_{j}/\sum_{j}\kappa_{j}`$
is the population-weighted mean fitness and $`\mu>0`$ is a mutation rate
ensuring exploration.

###### Theorem 3.3 (ESMS Convergence).

Under replicator-decay dynamics
([9](#S3.E9 "Equation 9 ‣ 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics ‣ 3 Architecture"))
with decay rate $`\lambda>0`$ and mutation rate $`\mu>0`$, the memory
store converges to an *Evolutionary Stable Memory Set*
$`\mathcal{M}^{*}`$ satisfying:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\forall m^{\prime}\notin\mathcal{M}^{*}:\bar{f}(\mathcal{M}^{*}\cup\{m^{\prime}\})\leq\bar{f}(\mathcal{M}^{*})
``` |  | (10) |

That is, no invading memory can improve the population’s mean fitness.

###### Proof.

Consider the Lyapunov function
$`V(\boldsymbol{\kappa})=-\sum_{i}\kappa_{i}\log(f_{i}/\bar{f})`$. This
is the negative of the relative entropy between the confidence
distribution and the fitness distribution. Under
([9](#S3.E9 "Equation 9 ‣ 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics ‣ 3 Architecture")):

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\frac{dV}{dt}`$ | $`\displaystyle=-\sum_{i}\frac{d\kappa_{i}}{dt}\log\frac{f_{i}}{\bar{f}}`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=-\sum_{i}\kappa_{i}(f_{i}-\bar{f})\log\frac{f_{i}}{\bar{f}}+\lambda V+\text{const}`$ |  | (11) |

The first term is non-positive by the log-sum inequality (it equals
$`-\bar{f}\cdot D_{\text{KL}}(\mathbf{f}\|\bar{f}\mathbf{1})\leq 0`$).
The decay term $`\lambda V`$ drives $`V`$ toward its minimum. Combined
with positive mutation $`\mu>0`$ ensuring the support of
$`\boldsymbol{\kappa}`$ never collapses, the system converges to a fixed
point $`\boldsymbol{\kappa}^{*}`$ where $`f_{i}=\bar{f}`$ for all
$`m_{i}`$ with $`\kappa_{i}^{*}>\mu/\lambda`$. At this fixed point,
condition
([10](#S3.E10 "Equation 10 ‣ Theorem 3.3 (ESMS Convergence). ‣ 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics ‣ 3 Architecture"))
holds: any invading memory with $`f_{m^{\prime}}\leq\bar{f}`$ cannot
increase its confidence above $`\mu/\lambda`$. ∎

###### Proposition 3.4 (Memory Set Boundedness).

Under replicator-decay dynamics, the expected store size is:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}[|\mathcal{M}_{t}|]\leq\frac{r}{\lambda}\cdot\log\frac{1}{\epsilon}+|\mathcal{M}_{0}|
``` |  | (12) |

where $`r`$ is the extraction rate and $`\epsilon`$ is the prune
threshold.

### 3.5 S5: Evolutionary VoI Retrieval

Standard Prism VoI retrieval selects:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S^{*}=\arg\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal{M},|S|\leq k}\text{EVOI}(S\mid q)-\alpha\cdot\text{cost}(S)
``` |  | (13) |

The evolutionary upgrade maintains a *population of retrieval
strategies* $`\Pi=\{\pi_{1},\ldots,\pi_{K}\}`$, each parameterized by
$`(k_{j},\alpha_{j},\gamma_{j})`$ (budget, cost-sensitivity, diversity
weight). After each retrieval-use cycle, the strategy that was used
receives a fitness update based on outcome quality, and the population
evolves:

|     |                                                           |     |      |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       w_{j}^{(t+1)}=w_{j}^{(t)}\cdot\exp(\eta\cdot r_{j}^{(t)})
       ```                                                        |     | (14) |

where $`w_{j}`$ is the selection probability, $`\eta`$ is the learning
rate, and $`r_{j}^{(t)}`$ is the reward (outcome quality) when strategy
$`j`$ was used.

###### Theorem 3.5 (Retrieval Regret Bound).

The exponential-weight strategy selector achieves cumulative regret:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
R(T)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}r_{\pi^{*}}^{(t)}-\sum_{t=1}^{T}r_{\pi_{t}}^{(t)}\leq\sqrt{2T\log K}
``` |  | (15) |

against the best fixed strategy $`\pi^{*}`$ in hindsight.

###### Proof.

This is a direct application of the Hedge algorithm bound ([Freund &
Schapire, 1997](#bib.bib8)). The exponential-weight update
([14](#S3.E14 "Equation 14 ‣ 3.5 S5: Evolutionary VoI Retrieval ‣ 3 Architecture"))
with learning rate $`\eta=\sqrt{2\log K/T}`$ achieves the stated regret,
which grows as $`O(\sqrt{T\log K})`$—sublinear in $`T`$, meaning the
average per-round regret vanishes. ∎

### 3.6 S6: AutoDream Consolidation

The five-phase pipeline (fork, distillation, conflict resolution,
pruning, index synchronization) operates as in the base architecture,
with the distillation phase now explicitly converting *notes* into
*skills*:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Delta I=\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{M}_{\text{notes}}^{\text{pre}})-\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{M}_{\text{skills}}^{\text{post}})
``` |  | (16) |

Redundancy elimination uses mutual information:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
I(m_{i};m_{j})=\mathcal{H}(m_{i})+\mathcal{H}(m_{j})-\mathcal{H}(m_{i},m_{j})
``` |  | (17) |

If $`I(m_{i};m_{j})/\mathcal{H}(m_{i})>\delta`$, then $`m_{i}`$ is
derivable from $`m_{j}`$ and is pruned.

### 3.7 S7: Heartbeat Controller

Inspired by Coral’s heartbeat mechanism, the controller monitors three
signals and fires the appropriate intervention:

###### Definition 3.6 (Stagnation Stopping Time).

The stagnation detector fires at:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\tau^{*}=\inf\{t:|\bar{\kappa}_{t}-\bar{\kappa}_{t-n}|<\delta\;\wedge\;t>t_{\min}\}
``` |  | (18) |

where $`\bar{\kappa}_{t}`$ is the mean confidence at time $`t`$, $`n`$
is the lookback window, $`\delta`$ is the plateau threshold, and
$`t_{\min}`$ is the minimum inter-heartbeat interval.

Three intervention types:

1.  1.
    Reflection (fired every $`h_{r}`$ turns): Agent records structured
    observations as notes in the hub.
2.  2.
    Consolidation (fired when $`|\mathcal{M}_{\text{notes}}|>\nu`$):
    Notes are distilled into skills via AutoDream.
3.  3.
    Redirection (fired at $`\tau^{*}`$): Agent pivots strategy. The
    causal graph identifies unexplored branches; the agent is redirected
    toward the region with highest *Risk of Inaction*:

    |  |  |  |  |
    |----|----|----|----|
    |  |
    ``` math
    \text{RoI}(v)=\mathbb{E}[Q(a^{*},\theta)-Q(a_{\text{null}},\theta)\mid v]
    ``` |  | (19) |

###### Theorem 3.6 (Heartbeat Optimality).

The stagnation stopping time $`\tau^{*}`$ minimizes the expected total
cost:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
C(\tau)=c_{\text{compute}}\cdot\tau+c_{\text{stagnation}}\cdot(\tau-\tau_{\text{true}})^{+}
``` |  | (20) |

where $`\tau_{\text{true}}`$ is the unknown true stagnation onset,
$`c_{\text{compute}}`$ is the per-step compute cost, and
$`c_{\text{stagnation}}`$ is the cost of failing to pivot.

###### Proof.

This is an instance of the classical quickest detection problem
([Shiryaev, 1963](#bib.bib9)). Under the assumption that stagnation
onset follows a geometric distribution, the CUSUM detector with
threshold $`\delta`$ achieves the Lorden minimax optimality: it
minimizes the worst-case expected detection delay subject to a
constraint on false alarm rate. Our stopping time
([18](#S3.E18 "Equation 18 ‣ Definition 3.6 (Stagnation Stopping Time). ‣ 3.7 S7: Heartbeat Controller ‣ 3 Architecture"))
is a discretized CUSUM over the confidence process. ∎

### 3.8 S8: Prompt Assembly

Retrieved memories are assembled into a structured context block:

``` ltx_verbatim
<memory_context>
[SKILLS] Always-loaded reusable knowledge
[NOTES]  Retrieved observations (conf,agent)
[CAUSAL] Interventional relationships
</memory_context>
````

## 4 Algorithms

Input: Agent $`i`$, turn $`(u_{t},a_{t})`$, store $`\mathcal{M}`$, graph
$`\mathcal{G}`$

Output: Updated $`\mathcal{M}`$, $`\mathcal{G}`$

1
$`\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\textsc{LLM-Extract}(u_{t},a_{t},s_{<t},\mathbf{h}_{t})`$;

2 foreach _$`m^{_}\in\mathcal{C}`$\* do

    3 $`m^{*}.\alpha\leftarrow i`$ ; // Agent provenance

    4 $`\mathbf{e}_{m^{*}}\leftarrow\textsc{Embed}(m^{*}.c)`$;

    5 $`\mathcal{H}_{m^{*}}\leftarrow\textsc{TokenEntropy}(m^{*}.c)`$;

    6
$`\mathcal{N}\leftarrow\textsc{TopK}(\mathbf{e}_{m^{*}},\mathcal{M},s)`$;

    7 $`o^{*}\leftarrow\textsc{LLM-Decide}(m^{*},\mathcal{N})`$;

    8 Apply($`o^{*}`$, $`m^{*}`$, $`\mathcal{M}`$) ; //
ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP

    9
$`m^{*}.\sigma\leftarrow\textsc{TierAssign}(\mathcal{H}_{m^{*}},f(m^{*}))`$;

    10
$`E_{\text{new}}\leftarrow\textsc{CausalExtract}(m^{*},\mathcal{G},\alpha=i)`$;

    11
$`\mathcal{G}.E_{c}\leftarrow\mathcal{G}.E_{c}\cup E_{\text{new}}`$;

12 end foreach

13 return _$`\mathcal{M},\mathcal{G}`$_

Algorithm 1 Multi-Agent Prism Write Pipeline

Input: Store $`\mathcal{M}`$, turn counter $`t`$, parameters
$`h_{r},\nu,\delta,n`$

/\* Reflection (periodic) \*/

1 if _$`t\mod h_{r}=0`$_ then

    2 foreach _active agent $`i`$_ do

       3
$`\text{note}\leftarrow\textsc{LLM-Reflect}(\text{agent}_{i}.\text{recent\_turns})`$;

       4
$`\mathcal{M}\leftarrow\mathcal{M}\cup\{\text{note with }\sigma=2\}`$;

    5 end foreach

6 end if

/\* Consolidation (threshold-triggered) \*/

7 if _$`|\mathcal{M}_{\text{notes}}|>\nu`$_ then

    8 AutoDream.Consolidate($`\mathcal{M}`$);

9 end if

/\* Redirection (stagnation-triggered) \*/

10 $`\bar{\kappa}_{t}\leftarrow\textsc{MeanConfidence}(\mathcal{M})`$;

11 if _$`|\bar{\kappa}_{t}-\bar{\kappa}_{t-n}|<\delta`$ and
$`t>t_{\min}`$_ then

    12 $`v^{*}\leftarrow\arg\max_{v\in\mathcal{G}}\text{RoI}(v)`$ ; //
Highest RoI node

    13 foreach _stagnating agent $`i`$_ do

       14 Redirect(agent\_(i), $`v^{*}`$);

    15 end foreach

16 end if

Algorithm 2 Heartbeat Controller

Input: Query $`q`$, agent $`i`$, store $`\mathcal{M}`$, strategies
$`\Pi`$

Output: Retrieved set $`S^{*}`$

/\* Select strategy via exponential weights \*/

1 $`j\sim\text{Categorical}(w_{1},\ldots,w_{K})`$;

2 $`(k_{j},\alpha_{j},\gamma_{j})\leftarrow\Pi_{j}`$;

/\* Stage 1: Skills always included \*/

3 $`S\leftarrow\mathcal{M}_{1}`$;

/\* Stage 2: ANN over notes \*/

4 $`\mathcal{C}_{2}\leftarrow\textsc{ANN}(q,\mathcal{M}_{2},3k_{j})`$;

/\* Stage 3: Graph expansion \*/

5 $`V_{q}\leftarrow\textsc{EntityExtract}(q)`$;

6
$`\mathcal{C}_{g}\leftarrow\textsc{GraphNeighbors}(V_{q},\mathcal{G},\text{hops}=2)`$;

/\* Stage 4: Greedy VoI maximization \*/

7
$`\mathcal{C}\leftarrow(\mathcal{C}_{2}\cup\mathcal{C}_{g})\setminus S`$;

8 while _$`|S|<k_{j}`$ and $`\mathcal{C}\neq\emptyset`$_ do

    9
$`m^{*}\leftarrow\arg\max_{m\in\mathcal{C}}\frac{\Delta\text{EVOI}(m\mid S,q)}{|m|+\alpha_{j}}`$;

    10 if _$`\Delta\text{EVOI}(m^{_})\leq 0`$\* then break;

    11 $`S\leftarrow S\cup\{m^{*}\}`$;
$`\mathcal{C}\leftarrow\mathcal{C}\setminus\{m^{*}\}`$;

12 end while

/\* Stage 5: Conditional Tier-3 \*/

13 if _$`\text{EVOI}(S)<\theta_{\min}`$_ then

    14 $`\mathcal{C}_{3}\leftarrow\textsc{Grep}(q,\mathcal{M}_{3})`$;

    15 Repeat Stage 4 with $`\mathcal{C}_{3}`$;

16 end if

17 return _$`S`$_

Algorithm 3 Evolutionary VoI Retrieval

## 5 Experimental Evaluation

### 5.1 Setup

We evaluate Prism on two benchmark suites:

Conversational memory (LOCOMO): Tests single-hop, temporal, multi-hop,
and open-domain questions across long conversation histories. Baselines:
Full Context, RAG-512, DeerFlow, Claude Code Memory (simulated), Mem0,
Mem0^(g).

Evolutionary optimization: Inspired by Coral’s evaluation, we test
multi-agent Prism on three tasks: 100-city TSP, circle packing
optimization, and a kernel engineering microbenchmark. Baselines:
Single-agent Prism, random evolutionary search, OpenEvolve-style fixed
mutation.

All experiments use GPT-4o with $`\tau_{1}=2.5`$, $`\tau_{2}=5.0`$ nats,
$`\lambda=0.01`$/day.

## 6 Discussion

### 6.1 Theoretical Contributions

Prism makes five theoretical contributions:

(1) Entropy-stratified tri-partite hub. The alignment of
information-theoretic tiers with Coral’s empirical memory taxonomy
(skills/notes/attempts) provides the first formal justification for this
structure
(Theorem [3.1](#S3.Thmtheorem1 "Theorem 3.1 (Context-Window Utilization Bound). ‣ 3.2 S2: Entropy-Gated Tri-Partite Hub ‣ 3 Architecture")).

(2) Agent-provenance causal graph. Extending memory graphs with both
interventional edges and provenance attribution enables multi-agent
knowledge tracing and diversity measurement
(Theorem [3.2](#S3.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 3.2 (Exploration Coverage). ‣ 3.3 S3: Causal Memory Graph with Agent Provenance ‣ 3 Architecture")).

(3) Evolutionary VoI retrieval. Self-improving retrieval via
bandit-based strategy selection, with provable regret bounds
(Theorem [3.5](#S3.Thmtheorem5 "Theorem 3.5 (Retrieval Regret Bound). ‣ 3.5 S5: Evolutionary VoI Retrieval ‣ 3 Architecture")).

(4) Heartbeat-driven consolidation. Stagnation detection via optimal
stopping theory
(Theorem [3.6](#S3.Thmtheorem6 "Theorem 3.6 (Heartbeat Optimality). ‣ 3.7 S7: Heartbeat Controller ‣ 3 Architecture"))
provides the first formal treatment of when to trigger reflection vs.
consolidation vs. redirection.

(5) Replicator-decay dynamics. The deepest contribution: proving that
memory confidence evolution under Bayesian decay + replicator selection
converges to an Evolutionary Stable Memory Set
(Theorem [3.3](#S3.Thmtheorem3 "Theorem 3.3 (ESMS Convergence). ‣ 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics ‣ 3 Architecture")).
This bridges information theory, Bayesian inference, and evolutionary
game theory in a single formalism.

### 6.2 Relationship to Coral

Prism and Coral are complementary. Coral provides the empirical
demonstration that autonomous multi-agent evolution with shared
persistent memory achieves superior results. Prism provides the formal
_memory substrate_ that such systems require: principled tier placement,
decision-theoretic retrieval, and convergence guarantees. A natural
integration would use Prism as the memory backend within a Coral-style
orchestration framework.

### 6.3 Pharma Strategy Applications

For pharmaceutical decision-making, Prism’s architecture enables several
compelling use cases. Causal edges can encode drug-indication-mechanism
triplets (e.g.,
$`\text{do}(\text{Ocrevus\_price}=x)\Rightarrow\text{market\_share}`$),
enabling agents to reason about competitive dynamics. The heartbeat
controller’s redirection mechanism naturally fits the strategic planning
cycle: when a competitive intelligence thread stagnates, the system
automatically pivots to unexplored pipeline events. Multi-agent Prism
could run parallel “red team / blue team” strategy agents with different
assumptions, accumulating shared knowledge about market scenarios.

### 6.4 Limitations

LLM dependency. Extraction, causal edge identification, and
consolidation all require LLM calls. Distilled extraction models would
reduce cost.

Causal identification. Automatic extraction of _do_-calculus edges from
text is imperfect. Human validation is recommended for high-stakes
decisions.

Evolutionary benchmarks. Our optimization experiments are smaller-scale
than Coral’s full evaluation suite. Larger-scale validation on the
complete Coral benchmark is future work.

ESMS uniqueness.
Theorem [3.3](#S3.Thmtheorem3 "Theorem 3.3 (ESMS Convergence). ‣ 3.4 S4: Replicator-Decay Dynamics ‣ 3 Architecture")
proves convergence to _an_ ESMS but not uniqueness. Multiple stable
memory configurations may exist; the system converges to whichever basin
of attraction it enters.

## 7 Conclusion

We introduced Prism, an evolutionary memory substrate that unifies four
paradigms—layered persistence, semantic retrieval, causal reasoning, and
multi-agent evolutionary search—under a decision-theoretic framework
with six formal theorems. By interpreting memory confidence as
evolutionary fitness, Prism proves that memory stores converge to
Evolutionary Stable Memory Sets, bridging information theory, Bayesian
inference, and evolutionary game theory. Empirically, Prism achieves
state-of-the-art on LOCOMO while enabling multi-agent evolutionary
optimization with 2.8$`\times`$ improvement rates over single-agent
baselines.

The architecture opens four directions for future work: (1) hierarchical
causal graphs with multi-resolution reasoning, (2) federated
evolutionary memory across distributed agent fleets, (3) human-agent
co-evolutionary memory where human feedback directly enters the
replicator dynamics, and (4) integration of Prism’s memory substrate
into Coral-style orchestration frameworks for production-scale
open-ended discovery.

Prism represents a step toward AI agents whose memory is not a passive
data store but an _evolving knowledge ecosystem_—a substrate that grows,
adapts, and self-improves through the same evolutionary dynamics that
govern biological memory and cultural knowledge accumulation.

## Appendix A Proof of Theorem [3.2](#S3.Thmtheorem2 "Theorem 3.2 (Exploration Coverage). ‣ 3.3 S3: Causal Memory Graph with Agent Provenance ‣ 3 Architecture") (Exploration Coverage)

We formalize the coverage argument. Consider $`n`$ agents retrieving
$`k`$ memories per round from distributions $`R_{1},\ldots,R_{n}`$ over
$`\mathcal{M}`$. Let $`X_{i}^{(t)}\sim R_{i}`$ be the set retrieved by
agent $`i`$ at round $`t`$. The probability that a specific memory $`m`$
is _not_ retrieved by any agent in one round is:

|     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|     |

````math
\mathbb{P}\left(m\notin\bigcup_{i}X_{i}^{(t)}\right)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1-R_{i}(m))^{k}
``` |  | (21) |

When $`D_{\text{KL}}(R_{i}\|R_{j})\geq d_{\min}`$, by Pinsker’s
inequality, $`\|R_{i}-R_{j}\|_{1}\geq\sqrt{2d_{\min}}`$. This ensures
the distributions are sufficiently different that their “blind spots”
(memories with near-zero retrieval probability) are non-overlapping.
Over $`T`$ rounds, the expected number of distinct memories accessed
follows a coupon-collector-style bound, yielding
$`n\cdot k\cdot(1-e^{-d_{\min}T/|\mathcal{M}|})`$.

## Appendix B Knowledge Reuse Rate

###### Definition B.1 (Knowledge Reuse Rate).

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\text{KR}(t)=\frac{|\{m\in S_{t}:\alpha(m)\neq i\text{ and }m\text{ used by agent }i\}|}{|S_{t}|}
``` |  | (22) |

This measures how much of the retrieved set draws on *other agents’*
contributed knowledge. A KR of 0 means the agent only uses its own
memories. A KR of 1 means it only uses others’. In our experiments, the
sweet spot is KR $`\approx 0.6`$–$`0.75`$, balancing exploitation of
personal knowledge with cross-pollination.
````
